quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You have a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Wait outside the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow other vehicles into the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait outside the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if traffic is blocking it, even if your light is green. If you enter and the light turns red, you will block other drivers. You can get a ticket for blocking the intersection.

questions.question: Why should you increase your distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers will try to pass before you.
Because you will get caught in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicle drivers cannot see you if you drive directly behind them. Increase your distance so you can see around the sides and see the road ahead.

questions.question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and brake hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Release the gas pedal to create space between you and the other vehicle. This is safer than slamming on the brakes or swerving.

questions.question: If you have a sudden tire blowout, what should you do?

options.text: Use the brakes gently.
Pump the brakes repeatedly.
Press the brakes hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes gently.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas and using light brake pressure.

questions.question: You arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles on your left and right. What do you do?

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until the intersection is clear before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Then proceed in the order vehicles arrived.

questions.question: You park uphill where there is no curb. After setting the parking brake, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Turn them toward the road edge.
Turn them away from the road edge.
Keep them straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them toward the road edge.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the road safely.

questions.question: A red light is showing, but a police officer directs you to go through the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions always take priority over traffic signals and signs. Follow the officer's instructions.

questions.question: When you see this sign, what does it mean?

options.text: A railroad crossing is ahead. Be ready to stop.
You must always stop at the railroad crossing.
Stop and wait for a signal before crossing the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing is ahead. Be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming. Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Wait for trains to pass before you proceed.

questions.question: You approach an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not entered yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a yellow light, prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, clear it quickly and safely.

questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it prevents a collision.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it prevents a collision.
questions.explanation: Never assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: When parallel parking facing downhill, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb or road edge.
Turn your wheels away from the curb or road edge.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb or road edge.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb. When parking uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb.

questions.question: How should you avoid glare from an oncoming car's headlights?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Look at the centerline of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Avoid looking at bright oncoming headlights by glancing toward the right side of the road. Then continue looking ahead to watch the other vehicle's position.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not permitted.
You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means you can cross it to pass another vehicle on the left if there is no oncoming traffic. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you and the driver on your left arrive at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
You have the right-of-way.
Whoever is signaling to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: Where should your hands be on the steering wheel to turn quickly?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other at the top of the steering wheel.
One at the top and one at the bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and helps you turn safely at high speeds.

questions.question: What should you do if an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights?

options.text: Look toward the center of the road.
Look toward the right side of the road.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded. This helps you see the road and stay on course. Do not keep your high beams on as retaliation.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Turn the wheels toward the curb.
Turn the wheels away from the curb.
Leave the wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels away from the curb when parking uphill on a street with a curb. Turn your wheels toward the curb when parking uphill without a curb or when parking downhill.

questions.question: When roads are slippery after rain starts, what should you do?

options.text: Avoid fast turns and stops.
Test your tire traction while going uphill.
Look less far ahead while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid fast turns and stops.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire traction, so drive slower than usual. Avoid making sharp turns or sudden stops at high speeds to prevent skidding.

questions.question: When can you legally make a left turn at a red light after stopping?

options.text: When turning from a two-way street onto a two-way street.
When turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
When you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you can turn left on red only when traveling on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street. Make sure there are no signs prohibiting the turn.

questions.question: How far away from a stop sign must you park?

options.text: At least 30 feet
At least 25 feet
At least 15 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 25 feet
questions.explanation: You cannot park within 25 feet of a stop sign at any time.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right, not a privilege.
Privilege, not a right.
Requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is not a right. You must earn it and keep it by following the rules.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, you should:

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Prepare to stop, if needed.
Maintain a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop, if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill. A vehicle might be stopped just out of sight. Slow down so you can stop if necessary.

questions.question: If cars keep passing you on both sides while you drive in the center lane of an expressway, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the lane on your right.
Move to the lane on your left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the lane on your right.
questions.explanation: Use the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than the traffic flow, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must turn right.
No right turns permitted.
Right turns permitted on a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns permitted.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Turning right at this intersection is illegal.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because you cannot see as well. Stay farther behind the car in front of you so you can stop if it stops suddenly. Use your headlights and follow the rules for high beams and low beams.
